memory_update.text: Highest-confidence public exposures for this node are operating nuclear fleet owners with signed hyperscaler PPAs or license-extension evidence: CEG, VST, DUK, SO.

Qualified supply-chain exposures worth tracking include BWXT, LEU, CCJ, GEV, CW, MIR, FLR, and J; these map to fuel/enrichment, reactor services, components, instrumentation, and EPC/engineering bottlenecks.

Advanced-reactor pure plays SMR, XE, and OKLO are directly relevant but should remain hypothesis-weighted until NRC licensing, fuel supply, binding offtake, project FID, and construction execution improve.

Evidence hierarchy for this node should prioritize NRC license actions, signed PPAs, restart milestones, uprate approvals, fuel/enrichment licenses, backlog, and named EPC/component awards over broad nuclear renaissance narratives.

Additional public-market screens should later evaluate D, ETR, PEG, NEE, AEP, BEP/BAM, EMR, FLS, AECOM, KBR, and uranium developers, but they were excluded here to keep the Layer 1B candidate set at 15.

node: Existing nuclear plants, uprates, life extensions, restart projects, SMRs, and nuclear EPC
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the nuclear generation and life-extension chokepoint. The highest-evidence public exposures are owners of operating nuclear fleets with license-extension, restart, PPA, or uprate optionality; next are fuel/enrichment and qualified nuclear component/service vendors; advanced-reactor pure plays are included but should be treated as higher-risk hypotheses unless backed by NRC milestones, binding offtake, fuel availability, and executable EPC structures.
